memory_update.text: ONTO should remain in the Layer 1 universe for the advanced-packaging metrology/inspection/process-control subnode; evidence strength is above average but requires revenue-mix validation.
FORM should remain in the Layer 1 universe for wafer-level test, probe cards, and known-good-die economics tied to chiplets, HBM, and advanced packaging.
PDFS is a lower-attention EDA-adjacent/yield-control software hypothesis; it needs proof that advanced-node or advanced-packaging complexity is translating into durable revenue growth.

Reference leaders ASML and KLA should be kept as context anchors, but future passes should avoid overfilling the list with mega-cap equipment names and instead test smaller niches such as mask inspection, e-beam review, reticle handling, probe-card materials, socket/test interfaces, and fab analytics.

node: Semiconductor equipment, EDA, metrology, inspection, and yield-control software
summary: Expanded the node around secondary semiconductor chokepoints beyond lithography. ASML and KLA remain reference anchors for lithography/process-control context, but the higher-value Layer 1B discovery lane is in narrower US-listed suppliers tied to advanced packaging inspection/metrology, wafer probe/test, and yield analytics. This pass prioritizes companies whose labels may understate their role in AI-chip manufacturability: Onto Innovation for advanced packaging process control, FormFactor for wafer probe cards and test interfaces, and PDF Solutions for manufacturing/yield analytics. No buy/sell view is expressed.
